item.title: Solved: How to Exit PDB and Allow Your Python Program to Continue
item.description: In the realm of Python programming, debugging is an indispensable skill, especially when dealing with computationally demanding applications. item.title: Solved: How to Show the Stack Trace from a Running Python Application
item.description:
In the realm of Python development, encountering a situation where your application becomes unresponsive can be frustrating, especially when the root cause isn’t immediately apparent. If you find yourself in this predicament, you might wonder: How can I obtain the current stack trace from a running Python application? The following is a comprehensive exploration of effective methods to achieve this, covering various scenarios and tools available for Python developers.

Top 8 Ways to Obtain the Stack Trace of a Running Python Application

Method 1: Installing a Signal Handler

One of the simplest ways to be able to diagnose issues is to use a signal handler. A classic example arises from a version control system such as Bazaar (bzr) , which by default configures a handler for SIGQUIT. When triggered, this invokes Python’s built-in debugger, pdb, allowing you to inspect the stack trace using the (w)here command.

item.title: Top 10 Methods to Print Object Properties and Values in Python
item.description:
Top 10 Methods to Print Object Properties and Values in Python

Debugging in Python often requires us to inspect an object’s properties and values. Unlike languages like PHP that offer functions like print_r(), Python provides several built-in functions and modules to achieve similar results. Below, we will explore various methods to effectively print all current properties and values of an object in Python, enhancing your debugging efforts.

Method 1: Using dir() and vars()

The simplest way to retrieve an object’s attributes is by using the dir() and vars() functions.
